notes: A Budapest Card or 24-hour ticket costs about 2,500 HUF. Tram 2 has views of both riverbanks. The 100E airport bus costs 2,200 HUF. Metro 1 is a historic line.

Summer temperatures are 28-32°C. The Sziget Festival is held in August (on an island in Óbuda). The baths' outdoor pools are a good option, boat evenings are cool, and there are fireworks on 20 August.
Baths cost 12-15,000 HUF (cheaper on weekdays), Parliament 10,000 and the synagogue 12,000. Renting towels and slippers is expensive, so bring your own.
Goulash (it's a soup!), pörkölt (stew), lángos, kürtőskalács, Dobos torta. Tip 10-12%, but check whether a 'szervizdíj' (service charge) has already been added to the bill.
Pay in cash in forints. Places that accept EUR give poor rates. Beware the 'no commission' trap at exchange offices, and at ATMs choose your own bank's rate.
The ruin pubs are around Kazinczy Street. The synagogue is closed on Saturdays and the Great Market Hall on Sundays.

stops.name: Fisherman's Bastion
stops.tips: Fairy-tale turrets and views over Parliament. The lower terraces are free; the upper tower costs 1,500 HUF (free before 08:00).

stops.name: Matthias Church
stops.tips: Colourful Zsolnay tiled roof. A coronation church with a mosaic interior.

stops.name: Buda Castle & Castle Hill Yürüyüşü
stops.tips: Palace courtyards and the Turul bird statue. The Hungarian National Gallery (4,400 HUF) is optional.

stops.name: Ruszwurm Cukrászda
stops.tips: The oldest pastry shop in the city (since 1827). Try the krémes (cream pastry); there are only 5 tables. Afterwards, take the funicular and walk across the Chain Bridge to Pest.

stops.name: Gerlóczy Kávéház
stops.tips: A Parisian-style café in Belváros, serving goulash and paprikás.

backups.name: Halászbástya Restaurant
backups.tips: Set inside Fisherman's Bastion with views, but expensive.

backups.name: Hospital in the Rock
backups.tips: A WWII hospital and nuclear bunker beneath the castle. Visits are by guided tour only.

stops.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
stops.tips: A 45-minute tour (including the Holy Crown). Book tickets online days ahead and don't forget your passport.

stops.name: St. Stephen's Basilica
stops.tips: Home to the mummified right hand of St Stephen. The dome panorama costs 3,000 HUF.

stops.name: Belvárosi Disznótoros
stops.tips: Hungarian butcher's food sold by weight: hurka (rice or liver sausage), kolbász (sausage), eaten standing up.

stops.name: Heroes' Square
stops.tips: Take Metro 1, the oldest metro on the continent. See the Millennium Monument and the seven tribal chieftains.

stops.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
stops.tips: Europe's largest thermal bath, in a yellow palace with a 38°C outdoor pool and chess tables. Bring your own slippers and towel; it's cheaper on weekdays.

backups.name: Gellért Thermal Bath
backups.tips: An Art Nouveau bath, as an alternative to Széchenyi.

backups.name: Vajdahunyad Vár Restoranı Városliget
backups.tips: A restaurant in the castle park.

stops.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
stops.tips: The largest synagogue in Europe, with the Weeping Willow memorial. Closed on Saturdays.

stops.name: Karaván Street Food
stops.tips: A food-truck courtyard next to Szimpla. Try lángos (fried dough with garlic and cheese) and kürtőskalács (chimney cake).

stops.name: Great Market Hall
stops.tips: An iron-framed market hall from 1897. Look for paprika and salami, with lángos on the upper floor. Closed on Sundays.

stops.name: Liberty Bridge & Gellért Hill
stops.tips: The green bridge, then a 30-minute climb up Gellért Hill for a Citadella panorama at sunset.

stops.name: Szimpla Kert
stops.tips: The original ruin bar (2002), with a bicycle café and a plant garden. Entry is free and a beer costs 1,000 HUF.

backups.name: Mazel Tov
backups.tips: A Middle Eastern garden restaurant in the Jewish Quarter. Book ahead.

backups.name: Hungarian National Museum
backups.tips: The steps where the 1848 revolution unfolded; an alternative to the market.

stops.name: Szentendre Fő tér
stops.tips: Take the HÉV train (40 minutes from Batthyány tér) to a Baroque artists' town with Serbian churches.

stops.name: Blagoveštenska Church Szentendre
stops.tips: A Serbian Orthodox church on the square.

stops.name: Aranysárkány Vendéglő
stops.tips: The town's classic restaurant, serving goulash and paprikás csirke (paprika chicken).

stops.name: Szentendre Tuna Kıyısı
stops.tips: A riverside walk. In summer you can return by boat (Mahart), taking 1.5 hours.

stops.name: Skanzen Open Air Museum
stops.tips: A museum of Hungarian village houses, 10 minutes by bus (April to October).

backups.name: Álom Lángos Szentendre
backups.tips: The town's famous lángos, from a small stand.

backups.name: Visegrád Castle
backups.tips: A castle on the Danube Bend, reached by bus; an alternative to Skanzen.

stops.name: Margaret Island
stops.tips: A park island in the Danube. Rent a bike or pedal cart, and see the musical fountain, Japanese garden and ruins.

stops.name: Andrássy Avenue
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed boulevard with the Opera, Liszt Square and luxury shops.

stops.name: Menza Liszt Ferenc tér
stops.tips: A retro Hungarian restaurant on Liszt Square. Try the goulash.

stops.name: House of Terror
stops.tips: The former Nazi and communist secret police headquarters. Heavy going but important. Closed on Mondays.

stops.name: Hungarian State Opera
stops.tips: A tour of the neo-Renaissance opera house (in English at 13:30 and 15:00), or evening tickets from 5,000 HUF.

backups.name: New York Café
backups.tips: Billed as 'the most beautiful café in the world'. Expect queues and high prices; an alternative to Menza.

backups.name: Miniversum
backups.tips: Miniature Hungarian model trains; an alternative to the House of Terror (with children).

stops.name: Aquincum Museum
stops.tips: Ruins of a Roman city in Óbuda, reached by HÉV.

stops.name: Lukács Thermal Bath
stops.tips: The locals' bath, quieter and cheaper than Széchenyi.

stops.name: Bambi Eszpresszó
stops.tips: A communist-era café unchanged since 1961, in Buda.

stops.name: Batthyány tér Parlamento Manzarası
stops.tips: The best view of Parliament, from across the river.

stops.name: Danube Sightseeing Cruise
stops.tips: A one-hour evening boat trip with the lights on. Parliament and the Castle glow like gold.

backups.name: Pesti Disznó
backups.tips: Modern Hungarian cooking with plenty of pork, in Pest.

backups.name: Óbuda Fő tér
backups.tips: Old Óbuda's square, with its statues of figures under umbrellas; an alternative to Aquincum.

stops.name: Váci Street
stops.tips: A pedestrian shopping street. Pick up paprika and Tokaji wine as souvenirs.

stops.name: Vörösmarty Square Gerbeaud
stops.tips: A pastry shop from 1858. Have Dobos torta and coffee as your farewell.

stops.name: Danube Promenade Little Princess
stops.tips: The Little Princess statue, and tram line 2 running along the riverbank.

stops.name: Deák Ferenc tér 100E Havalimanı Otobüsü
stops.tips: The direct 100E bus takes 40 minutes. Farewell.

backups.name: Café Central Budapest
backups.tips: A literary café from 1887; an alternative to Gerbeaud.

backups.name: Erzsébet tér Ferris Wheel
backups.tips: The Budapest Eye Ferris wheel; an alternative to the river.
